issues.legal_issue: A statement referring to a mortgage relationship restarts limitation only if it is intended to acknowledge the subsisting right to redeem and the corresponding liability to be redeemed.
material_facts: The claimants brought a suit seeking redemption and possession of their share of mortgaged property after the applicable sixty-year limitation period had expired.

They relied on earlier deeds and pleadings that referred to the mortgage relationship. The deeds and plaint referred to the mortgage rights to describe interests being mortgaged, sold, or asserted; the written statement denied the claimants’ right to redeem.
The Court found that none of the statements was intended to acknowledge a subsisting liability to permit redemption.
issues.conclusion: The statements were not acknowledgments capable of saving the suit from limitation. The suit was barred, and the appeal was dismissed.
issues.legal_principle: Under Section 19 of the Limitation Act, 1908, an acknowledgment must be in writing, signed by the party against whom the right is claimed or a person through whom that party derives title or liability, and made before expiry of the limitation period. Explanation 1 means the acknowledgment need not specify the exact nature of the right, but it must relate to a subsisting liability. Applying Shapur Fredoom Mazda v. Durga Prosad, the Court held that the words and circumstances must show an intention to admit the subsisting jural relationship; that intention may be inferred, but cannot be imposed by strained reasoning. A reference to mortgage status made merely to describe rights in a transaction, or in a pleading that denies redemption, does not by itself establish the required acknowledgment. The Court also referred to Green v. Humphreys on the need for an admission that the writer owed the liability.

rule.if: redemption_proceeding and limitation_period_expired and writings_referred_to_mortgage_status and writings_were_descriptive_or_denied_redemption and no_intent_to_admit_subsisting_liability

predicates.redemption_proceeding: The claimant brought a proceeding seeking redemption of mortgaged property.
predicates.limitation_period_expired: The applicable limitation period had elapsed before the claimant filed the proceeding.
predicates.writings_referred_to_mortgage_status: Earlier writings attributable to the opposing side or its predecessors referred to a mortgage relationship.
predicates.writings_were_descriptive_or_denied_rede: The writings used the mortgage references to describe interests being dealt with or asserted, or denied the claimant’s right to redeem.
predicates.no_intent_to_admit_subsisting_liability: The writers did not intend to admit that a current liability to permit redemption subsisted.

issues.definition: When a redemption proceeding is filed after the limitation period has expired, references to mortgage status made descriptively or alongside a denial of redemption, without intent to admit a subsisting liability, leave the redemption claim time-barred.
